themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 14 this week, a 195% increase over the 8-week baseline of 4.8 complaints per week, signaling a sudden environmental and quality-of-life crisis in Far Rockaway.
evidence: 14 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.58)
195% spike represents a sudden acceleration, not a gradual trend
Aligns with broader sanitation concerns (unsanitary conditions rank #8 overall at 366 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Interview residents on affected blocks to document what is being dumped and where; map hotspots
Contact DSNY and environmental enforcement to understand why this week's spike occurred and what enforcement actions are planned

themes_detail.label: Facility & Infrastructure Maintenance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance and facility complaints jumped to 10 this week, a 196% increase over the 3.4 weekly baseline, suggesting deteriorating public infrastructure across the district during the same week as illegal dumping spike.
evidence: 10 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.04)
196% spike is most recent deviation, appearing same week as illegal dumping acceleration
Long-standing infrastructure concerns reflected in repeated CB budget requests for DEP capital projects and street sewer development
reporting_angles: Obtain specific 311 complaint descriptions to identify which facilities (parks, public buildings, transit stops) are most affected
Cross-reference with DOB permits (406 filings in last 90 days, mostly alterations) to determine if construction is exacerbating maintenance backlog

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicle Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints spiked to 20 last week, a 191% increase over the 6.9 weekly baseline, indicating a rapid worsening of abandoned vehicle problem that compounds illegal parking concerns (1,103 complaints over 90 days).
evidence: 20 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.59)
Abandoned vehicles rank #9 overall at 264 complaints over 90 days; spike suggests rapid acceleration
Converges with illegal parking (#3 complaint type, 1,103 total) to suggest broader vehicle management crisis
reporting_angles: Identify which streets/blocks have the highest concentration of derelict vehicles and document condition with photos
Interview NYPD and Sanitation Department on towing capacity and timeline for removal; ask why response may be delayed

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 5 two weeks ago from a near-zero baseline (0.2 weekly average), a statistically extreme 1900% spike indicating sudden emergence of vacant lot or yard blight issues.
evidence: 5 lot condition complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.97, highest severity)
1900% spike is most dramatic statistical anomaly in dataset but appears to be one-week event
May signal sudden property abandonment or deterioration tied to waterfront development activity (5 active ULURP/zoning applications pending)
reporting_angles: Map the 5 complaints to specific addresses and determine if they cluster around active development projects or distinct neighborhoods
Investigate whether development displacement or speculation is contributing to lot abandonment; interview affected property owners

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Emergence
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 6 last week, a 129% increase over the 2.6 weekly baseline, suggesting new business activity or venue operations adding nuisance noise pressure on residential areas.
evidence: 6 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.4)
Residential noise also high overall (1,106 complaints over 90 days, #2 category), suggesting noise is endemic issue
Spike may correlate with seasonal business reopening or new commercial activity in warming months
reporting_angles: Identify which businesses/venues generated the 6 complaints and what type of noise (music, construction, loading)
Interview neighbors and Community Board about quality-of-life friction between emerging commercial uses and residential district character
